small_guidance:
- The conv tile materializes `HCONV*WCONV` = (BLOCK_PH*4)*(BLOCK_PW*4) elements per program (e.g. 16x32=512 for BLOCK_PH=4,BLOCK_PW=8), which inflates register pressure and shared accumulator size. Add autotune configs with smaller pool tiles like `BLOCK_PH=1, BLOCK_PW=4` and `BLOCK_PH=2, BLOCK_PW=4` (HCONV/WCONV = 4x16, 8x16) paired with larger `BLOCK_OC=128` to improve weight reuse.
- Hoist the weight load out of the `ic/kh/kw` loop tail: preload the full `[BLOCK_OC, IC*KH*KW]` weight tile once (IC=8, KH=KW=3 → 72 elements per OC) into registers, then iterate over ic/kh/kw using indexing — eliminates 72 redundant weight loads per program.
- The `tl.where(valid, val, -inf)` masking is redundant since `load_mask` already zeros invalid input contributions; since OH/OW (254) are not multiples of POOL=4 only at the very edge tile, drop the valid mask when the tile is fully inside (use a compile-time fast path) or just keep `load_mask` zeroing — saves shape-juggling overhead.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an explicit im2col-style GEMM layout where each program computes a `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_M]` tile of conv output with `BLOCK_M` covering a contiguous run of pooled-output positions (one row of pool windows = POOL*BLOCK_PW conv columns). Accumulate via `tl.dot` over a K dimension of `IC*KH*KW`, which lets tensor cores be used (fp32 → tf32) instead of the current outer-product scalar FMAs — this is the main headroom on Ada.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout: permute `x` to `(N, IH, IW, IC)` once on the host, so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) has IC contiguous, enabling vectorized 128-bit loads of the im2col gather. Weights similarly stored as `(OC, KH, KW, IC)`.
- Make the kernel persistent over the OC dimension or the spatial tile dimension so a single program reuses the same input/weight rows for multiple OC blocks — reduces redundant input reads since the conv tile is the same for every OC tile at a given spatial location.
